title: Five Questions Before Signing a Commercial Lease in Newcastle
excerpt: Turn a proposed lease into a clear list of commercial questions and adviser actions. Check the costs, premises requirements and future business needs before committing.
author: Joe Kelley
metaTitle: Before Signing a Commercial Lease Newcastle | YOS
metaDescription: Prepare useful questions about occupancy costs, exit obligations, rent reviews, intended use and flexibility before your Newcastle commercial lease decision.
body:
## What should you clarify before signing a commercial lease?

Understand the commercial proposal, the premises requirements and the commitments your business is considering. These five questions help organise the brief and the information still needed. They do not replace your solicitor's review of the actual documents.

For a Newcastle or Hunter business, bring the proposed terms, available building information, current lease position and operating requirements into the same discussion. Avoid comparing headline rent while leaving setup costs or exit obligations unexamined.

## 1. What is included in the occupancy cost?

Request the proposed rent, available outgoings information, review arrangements and other stated premises costs. Record what is included, what is additional, the GST basis and the source of each figure. Ask your solicitor and accountant to clarify the proposed obligations and budget implications.

**Helpful tip:** use one comparison sheet for each option. Keep ongoing occupancy costs separate from FitOut, furniture, moving and other initial expenditure.

[Organise assumptions in the lease comparison tool](/resources/lease-comparison)

## 2. What needs to happen when the lease ends?

Ask your solicitor to explain any make-good, removal or reinstatement wording and how it relates to the premises condition and proposed works. Gather available condition records, plans and correspondence before asking contractors to estimate work.

Do not assume a generic cost per square metre establishes your obligation or budget. Clarify the scope first, then obtain project-specific inputs.

**Helpful tip:** maintain a list of unresolved items with a document reference and an owner. Separate a proposed commercial arrangement from one that has been agreed and documented.

[Prepare a make-good scope and budget](/blog/make-good-obligations-commercial-lease-cost)

## 3. How will the rent be reviewed?

Identify the proposed review method and dates, then ask your solicitor to explain the wording and any conditions. Model commercial scenarios with clear assumptions rather than assuming the starting rent remains unchanged.

Do not treat a floor, cap or other review clause as automatically favourable. Have the effect and suitability of the proposed terms assessed for your transaction.

**Helpful tip:** show which inputs are contractual, proposed or illustrative. A forecast is easier to assess when uncertain assumptions are visible.

[Read the commercial lease comparison guide](/blog/how-to-compare-commercial-leases)

## 4. Does the premises suit the intended activities?

Describe the actual activities, equipment, access, servicing and visitor needs. Ask the appointed advisers to assess the proposed use, building constraints, landlord requirements and relevant approval pathway for the actual site.

Connect this work with the workplace layout, likely changes and operating date. Do not assume a listing description or existing fit out establishes suitability for your business.

**Helpful tip:** bring the business brief and available floor plan to the same conversation. Identify which questions need specialist assessment before commitment.

[Explore client-side office FitOut planning](/office-fitout)

## 5. What happens if the business needs change?

Discuss possible growth, downsizing, a sale or relocation with your advisers. Ask your solicitor to explain any renewal, transfer, subletting or early-exit provisions and the conditions attached. Their availability or outcome should not be assumed.

Confirm who can approve the commercial decision, which documents need review and the next action required from each party.

**Helpful tip:** record the dates and dependencies affecting the decision. Ask your solicitor to confirm notice requirements against the documents rather than using a generic deadline.

[Organise confirmed lease dates](/tools/critical-dates)

## Bring the questions into a useful brief

[Explore Newcastle tenant representation](/tenant-rep/newcastle) or [compare Tenant Rep packages](/tenant-rep#packages). YOS confirms scope and fees before engagement; your solicitor provides legal advice.

[Start a free Lease Health Check](/lease-health-check) with your lease situation and timing. Uploading your current lease is optional and further advisory work is scoped separately.

[Send your leasing enquiry](#blog-contact-form) if you want help clarifying the next commercial decision.

## Official guidance and its scope

The NSW Small Business Commissioner recommends obtaining legal advice before entering a lease.

The linked NSW retail leasing guidance should not be assumed to apply to every office or industrial lease. Ask your solicitor which requirements apply to your premises and transaction.

[NSW Small Business Commissioner: before you sign the lease](https://www.smallbusiness.nsw.gov.au/help/common-questions/before-you-sign-the-lease)

[NSW Small Business Commissioner: understanding leasing costs](https://www.smallbusiness.nsw.gov.au/help/common-questions/understanding-the-costs-of-leasing)
